description: Repo-scale (springboot-tasktracker): POST /tasks/bulk-assign must reject the whole batch if the CUMULATIVE active-task count would exceed the assignee's cap - not check each task against a stale pre-batch baseline
prompts: Add `POST /tasks/bulk-assign`: body `{"taskIds": [...], "assigneeId": N}`, assigning every given task to that user in one call. It must be atomic: validate the assignee exists AND every taskId refers to an existing task BEFORE assigning any of them (404 if any is missing, nothing assigned). Enforce a capacity limit: an assignee may have at most 3 'active' tasks (status TODO or IN_PROGRESS) at once. Critically, get the capacity check right: the invariant is that the assignee's active-task count (existing + everything in this batch, combined) must never exceed the cap. Compute the assignee's current active count and compare `current + taskIds.size()` against the cap ONCE for the whole batch - do not check each task individually against the pre-batch count, since that lets a batch of several tasks sail past a cap that would reject them if counted together. Reject the entire batch (nothing assigned) with 409 if it would overflow. Add a `ConflictException` (409) alongside the existing `NotFoundException`, wired into `ApiExceptionHandler`.
name: add_springboot_tasktracker_bulk_assign_cumulative_capacity
